There are two problems with KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG.  First
it can take kvm->mmu_lock for an extended period of time.  Second
can actually see many false positives in some cases.  The latter is due
to a benign race like this:
1. KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG returns a set of dirty pages and write protects
them.
2. The guest modifies the pages
column2: causing them to be marked ditry.

column1: 3. Userspace actually copies the pages.
4. KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG returns those pages as dirty again
they were not written to since (3).
This is especially a problem for large guests
(1) and (3) can be substantial.  This patch introduces a new
capability which
write-protect the pages it returns.  Instead
explicitly clear the dirty log bits just before using the content
of the page.  The new KVM_CLEAR_DIRTY_LOG ioctl can also operate on a
64-page granularity rather than requiring to sync a full memslot;
this way
column2: the mmu_lock is taken for small amounts of time

column1: only a small amount of time will pass between write protection
of pages and the sending of their content.
